frozen_evidence_boundary: repository source only; no issues/PRs before freeze
raw_signal_observation: RegisterOidcProvider lowercases the configured provider name; if that normalized key already exists, it logs a warning and overwrites the previous oidcProviders entry.
material_claim: Two configured OIDC providers whose names differ only by case collapse to one runtime registration. The overwrite behavior is locally established; whether collision should fail closed, warn-and-overwrite, or be otherwise permitted is product/operator intent rather than a defect established by source alone.
required_reality_floor: R1 for overwrite behavior; OWNER for whether overwrite is acceptable product policy
neta_next_move: Do not change collision behavior from source inspection alone. Ask for/locate explicit maintainer intent for case-colliding provider names; if intent is fail-closed, add a config validation gate with a deliberate duplicate-case positive control.
reversal_condition: If maintainer intent or an existing contract states that last-registration-wins is intended, retain behavior. If it requires unique provider identity, promote to BUILD_READY with a failing duplicate-normalization test first.
baseline_decision: BUILD: reject duplicate provider names after case normalization instead of overwriting the earlier registration; return a startup/configuration error.

evidence: The pinned source explicitly logs that normalized duplicate registration overwrites the previous provider, demonstrating the behavior is deliberate enough to be named rather than an accidental map side effect.

Issue search after freeze found OIDC product-intent discussion (#897) where the contributor explicitly asks maintainers before coding login-flow behavior; no issue/bug report was found establishing that case-colliding provider names must be rejected.
adjudication.decision_delta: Neta prevented an immediate policy-changing build that the baseline recommended. Adjudication supports restraint: the local overwrite is real, but repository/user evidence did not establish that overwrite violates intended product policy.
adjudication.lesson: A deterministic local behavior can be fully established while the normative question of whether it is a defect remains OWNER authority. Code certainty is not change permission.
